literal_edit.before: at every point the stars of the finitely many simplices containing it give a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets with the explicit conical product charts.
literal_edit.after: at a point in the relative interior of a retained simplex $\sigma$, its open star is a neighbourhood with chart $\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(L)$ taking the point to $(p,\mathrm{apex})$. Shrink the first factor to convex open neighbourhoods of $p$ and the second to cones of radius $0<\epsilon<1$. Compactness of $L$ gives uniform radial neighbourhoods at the apex, so these products form a neighbourhood basis; each is contractible by straight-line contraction of the first factor and radial contraction of the cone. The same basis restricted to any open subset proves its local contractibility.
